title: Duguma Wins Millrose 1000m, Hurta-Klecker 4th
excerpt: Tsige Duguma won the 2026 Millrose 1000m in a world-leading 2:35.50; Sage Hurta-Klecker was fourth. Pacing lessons for stepping up in distance.
body:
Olympic 800m silver medalist Tsige Duguma won the women's 1000m at the 2026 Millrose Games in a world-leading 2:35.50, ahead of Addy Wiley (2:35.77) and Maggi Congdon (2:35.91). Sage Hurta-Klecker, who headlined the race with Duguma, finished fourth in 2:36.76.

Jen Toomey's American indoor record of 2:34.19 was not threatened. Hurta-Klecker had said before the meet that she was not treating the race as a record attempt.

The 1000m is a step up for 800m specialists, and stepping up in distance usually means starting a little slower than your instincts tell you. Before your next race at an unfamiliar distance, run the first quarter of the distance at your target pace in training. If that feels uncomfortable, your planned race pace is probably too aggressive.

Sources: LetsRun.com preview; LetsRun.com results
keyTakeaway: When you step up in distance, start at a pace you can hold, not the pace of your shorter event.
